title: The energy that becomes thermal
target: Account for mechanical energy changes through heating and deformation.
criteria: Track system boundaries in an energy balance.
Use energy differences to quantify a transfer.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A block slides across a rough floor. Which system can contain the friction-related internal-energy increase in both surfaces?
options: The block with all floor interactions ignored.
Only the ruler used to measure distance.
cpa.guide: The system boundary should include the interacting surfaces when counting their internal energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Mechanical energy leaves a selected system through heating. What must the energy account include?
options: An energy transfer across its boundary.
An automatic increase in kinetic energy.
A violation of total energy conservation.
cpa.guide: Energy can cross a chosen system boundary; the account must track it.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which distinction between temperature and internal energy is correct?
options: A warmer tiny sample must store more internal energy than any large sample.
Equal temperatures always imply equal total internal energies.
Temperature is not the same quantity as total internal energy.
cpa.guide: Internal energy also depends on amount and material; temperature alone is insufficient.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two samples of the same material have equal mass and initial temperature. One receives twice the heating energy, with constant heat capacity and no phase change. Compare temperature rises.
options: The twice-heated sample has twice the rise.
Its rise is four times as large.
cpa.guide: With identical mc, ΔT = Q/(mc) scales with Q.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A constant 6 N friction force opposes a 4 m slide. What is friction’s work on the block?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A system receives 50 J. Its motion energy rises 18 J and its internal energy rises 27 J. If no other stored form changes, how much energy leaves the system?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
